1. Qf5+ {The queen gives check, at the adverse king's bishop's fourth square. (a) NOTE: To win
this game, the queen must be previously brought, as near as possible, to the adverse king.} Kg2
{The king, at the adverse king's knight's second square.} 2. Qg4+ {The queen gives check, at her
king's knight's fourth square.} Kf2 {The king, at the adverse king's bishop's second square.} 3.
Qf4+ {The queen gives check, at her king's bishop's fourth square.} Kg2 {The king, at the
adverse king's knight's second square.} 4. Qe3 {The queen, at her king's third square.} Kf1 {The
king, at the adverse king's bishop's square. (b) NOTE: It is this move which enables you to win
the game, because you force him to play his king under his pawn.} 5. Qf3+ {The queen gives
check, at her king's bishop's third square.} Ke1 {The king, at the adverse king's square. (c)
NOTE: As his pawn cannot make a queen, you must make a good use of this instant to bring your
king next to his.} 6. Kc6 {The king, at the adverse queen's bishop's third square.} Kd2 {The
king, at the adverse queen's second square.} 7. Qd5+ {The queen gives check, at the adverse
queen's fourth square.} Kc2 {The king, at the adverse queen's bishop's second square.} 8. Qc4+
{The queen gives check, at her bishop's fourth square.} Kd2 {The king, at the adverse queen's
second square.} 9. Qd4+ {The queen gives check, at her fourth square.} Kc2 {The king, at the
adverse queen's bishop's second square.} 10. Qe3 {The queen, at her king's third square. (d)
NOTE: It is always the same move, which forces him to play his king under his pawn.} Kd1 {The
king, at the adverse queen's square.} 11. Qd3+ {The queen gives check, at her third square.} Ke1
{The king, at the adverse king's square.} 12. Kd5 {The king, at the adverse queen's fourth
square. (e) NOTE: You will proceed with the same moves till your king comes next to his pawn,
and then the game is won.} *
